question.text: Mr. Rajesh Menon is setting up 'Aravali Opportunities AIF' as a trust structure. The settlor conveys the initial corpus to the trustee. Which document is the foundational instrument that brings this trust into existence and also serves as the instrument of trusteeship?

answer.text: The Private Placement Memorandum filed with SEBI
The Trust Indenture (Trust Deed) executed between settlor and trustee
The Investment Management Agreement between trustee and manager
The Contribution Agreement between trustee and first investor

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.2 of the chapter, when an AIF is constituted as a trust, a 'Trust Indenture' is executed between the settlor and the trustee to bring the trust into existence. It is also the instrument of trusteeship and is required to be registered under AIF Regulations. The trust document establishes the determinate status of corpus for tax treatment under the Income Tax Act, 1961. The Trap: PPM is an offer document filed with SEBI, not a constitutional document. The IMA governs manager's appointment, not the trust's existence. Contribution Agreement governs the investor's subscription, not the trust's formation. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/XIX-B Distributor exams test PPM features at surface level. XIX-C Manager perspective requires distinguishing constitutional (Trust Deed) vs contractual (IMA, Contribution Agreement) vs disclosure (PPM) documents. Manager's Pro-Tip: While settling the trust, always ensure the corpus is 'determinate' (named beneficiaries identifiable) — failure to do so risks the trust being taxed at maximum marginal rate rather than pass-through under Section 115UB.
